intro.title: Book Introduction - Habakkuk
intro.html:
Book Introduction - Habakkuk

It seems most probable that Habakkuk prophesied in the latter years of Josiah. Of the prophet himself nothing is known. To him the character of Jehovah was revealed in terms of the highest spirituality. He alone of the prophets was more concerned that the holiness of Jehovah should be vindicated than that Israel should escape chastisement. Written just upon the eve of the captivity, Habakkuk was God’s testimony to Himself as against both idolatry and pantheism.

The book is in five parts:

1. Habakkuk’s perplexity in view of the sins of Israel and the silence of God, 2Ki 1:1-4.

2. Historically this was the time of Jehovah’s forbearance because of Josiah’s repentance (2Ki 22:18-20).

3. The answer of Jehovah to the prophet’s perplexity 2Ki 1:5-11.

4. The prophet, thus answered, utters the testimony to Jehovah, 2Ki 1:12-17; but he will watch for further answers, 2Ki 2:1.

5. To the watching prophet comes the response of the "vision," 2Ki 2:20. All ends in Habakkuk’s sublime Psalm of the Kingdom.

As a whole the Book of Habakkuk raise and answers the question of God’s consistency with Himself in view of permitted evil. The prophet thought that the holiness of God forbade him to go on with evil Israel. The answer of Jehovah announces a Chaldean invasion (Hab 1:6), and a world- wide dispersion Hab 1:5). But Jehovah is not mere wrath; "He delighteth in mercy" (Mic 7:18), and introduces into His answers to the perplexed prophet the great promises, Hab 1:5; Hab 2:3; Hab 2:4; Hab 2:14; Hab 2:20.

verses.text: Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention.

verses.text: Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.

verses.text: Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you.

footnotes.text: Hab 1:5 anticipates the dispersion "among the nations" (cf) Deu 28:64-67. While Israel as a nation is thus dispersed, Jehovah will "work a work" which Israel "will not believe." Act 13:37-41, interprets this prediction of the redemptive work of Christ. It is significant that Paul quotes this to Jews of the dispersion in the synagogue at Antioch.

footnotes.text: To the watching prophet comes the response of the "vision" Hab 2:2-20). Three elements are to be distinguished: (1) The moral judgment of Jehovah upon the evils practised by dispersed Israel (Hab 5-13,15-19). (2) The future purpose of God that, practised by dispersed Israel (Hab 2:5-13; Hab 2:15-19). (2) The future purpose of God that, "the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea" (Hab 2:14). That this revelation awaits the return of the Lord in glory is shown (a) by the parallel passage in Isa 11:9-12 and (b) by the quotation of Hab 2:3 in Heb 10:37; Heb 10:38 where the "it" of the "vision" becomes "he" and refers to the return of the Lord. It is then, after the "vision" is fulfilled, that "the knowledge of the glory," etc, shall fill the earth. But (3) meantime, "the just shall live by his faith." This great evangelic word is applied to Jew and Gentile in Rom 1:17 to the Gentiles in Gal 3:11-14 and to Hebrews (especially) in Heb 10:38. This opening of life to faith alone, makes possible not only the salvation of the Gentiles during the dispersion of Israel "among the nations"; Hab 1:5; Gal 3:11-14 but also makes possible a believing remnant in Israel while the nation, as such, is in blindness and unbelief, (See Scofield " Rom 11:1 ") with neither priesthood nor temple, and consequently unable to keep the ordinances of the law. Such is Jehovah! In disciplinary government His ancient Israel is cast out of the land and judicially blinded 2Co 3:12-15 but in covenanted mercy the individual Jew may resort to the simple faith of Abraham; Gen 15:6; Rom 4:1-5 and be saved. But this does not set aside the Palestinian See Scofield "Deu 30:3" and Davidic See Scofield "2Sa 7:16". Covenants, for "the earth shall be filled," etc. (Hab 2:14),and Jehovah will again be in His temple (Hab 2:20). Cf.; Hab 2:14; Hab 2:20; Rom 11:25-27

footnotes.text: Sheol is, in the O.T., the place to which the dead go. (1) Often, therefore, it is spoken of as the equivalent of the grave, merely, where all human activities cease; the terminus toward which all human life moves (e.g. Gen 42:38 grave Job 14:13 grave Psa 88:3 grave (2) To the man "under the sun," the natural man, who of necessity judges from appearances, sheol seems no more than the grave-- the end and total cessation, not only of the activities of life, but of life itself. Ecc 9:5; Ecc 9:10 (3) But Scripture reveals sheol as a place of sorrow 2Sa 22:6; Psa 18:5; Psa 116:3; in which the wicked are turned Psa 9:17 and where they are fully conscious; Isa 14:9-17; Eze 32:21 see, especially, Jon 2:2 what the belly of the great fish was to Jonah that sheol is to those who are therein). The sheol of the O.T. and hades of the N.T. (See Scofield " Luk 16:23 ") are identical.

footnotes.keyword: For the earth shall be filled
footnotes.text: Cf. Isa 11:9 which fixes the time when "the earth," etc. It is when David’s righteous Branch has set up the kingdom. (See "Kingdom (O.T.),"; 2Sa 7:9; Zec 12:8 also, "Kingdom (N.T.),"; Luk 1:31-33; 1Co 15:28. Habakkuk’s phrase marks an advance on that of Isaiah. In the latter it is "the knowledge of the Lord." That, in a certain sense, is being diffused now; but in Habakkuk it is "the knowledge of the glory of the Lord," and that cannot be till He is manifested in glory; Mat 24:30; Mat 25:31; Luk 9:26; 2Th 1:7; 2Th 2:8; Jud 1:14. The transfiguration was a foreview of this. Luk 9:26-29.

footnotes.keyword: For the earth shall be filled
footnotes.text: Cf. Isa 11:9 which fixes the time when "the earth," etc. It is when David’s righteous Branch has set up the kingdom. (See "Kingdom (O.T.),"; 2Sa 7:9; Zec 12:8 also, "Kingdom (N.T.),"; Luk 1:31-33; 1Co 15:28. Habakkuk’s phrase marks an advance on that of Isaiah. In the latter it is "the knowledge of the Lord." That, in a certain sense, is being diffused now; but in Habakkuk it is "the knowledge of the glory of the Lord," and that cannot be till He is manifested in glory; Mat 24:30; Mat 25:31; Luk 9:26; 2Th 1:7; 2Th 2:8; Jud 1:14. The transfiguration was a foreview of this. Luk 9:26-29.

footnotes.text: Prayer in the O.T. is in contrast with prayer in the N.T. in two respects: (1) In the former the basis of prayer is a covenant of God, or an appeal to his revealed character as merciful, gracious, etc. In the latter the basis is relationship: "When ye pray, say, Our Father" Mat 6:9. (2) A comparison, e.g. of the prayers of Moses and Paul, will show that one was praying for an earthly people whose dangers and blessings were earthly; the other for a heavenly people whose dangers and blessings were spiritual.

verses.text: O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.
verses.marked_text: O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.

verses.text: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.
verses.marked_text: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.

verses.text: And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power.
verses.marked_text: And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand: and there was the hiding of his power.

verses.text: Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet.
verses.marked_text: Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet.

verses.text: He stood, and measured the earth: he beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.
verses.marked_text: He stood, and measured the earth: he beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.

verses.text: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction: and the curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.
verses.marked_text: I saw the tents of Cushan<fn n="2"/> in affliction: and the curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.

footnotes.text: Or, Ethiopia.

Cushan

Or, Ethiopia.

verses.text: Was the Lord displeased against the rivers? was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?
verses.marked_text: Was the Lord displeased against the rivers? was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?

verses.text: Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word. Selah. Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.
verses.marked_text: Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word. Selah. Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.

verses.text: The mountains saw thee, and they trembled: the overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, and lifted up his hands on high.
verses.marked_text: The mountains saw thee, and they trembled: the overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, and lifted up his hands on high.

verses.text: The sun and moon stood still in their habitation: at the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear.
verses.marked_text: The sun and moon stood still in their habitation: at the light<fn n="3"/> of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear.

at the light

verses.text: Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.
verses.marked_text: Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.

verses.text: Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed; thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked, by discovering the foundation unto the neck. Selah.
verses.marked_text: Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed; thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked, by discovering the foundation unto the neck. Selah.

verses.text: Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me: their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.
verses.marked_text: Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me: their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.

verses.text: Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, through the heap of great waters.
verses.marked_text: Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, through the heap of great waters.

verses.text: When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.
